body:
Cole Summers: heads up: reconciliation variance alert just fired for unit-econ daily rollup. spike on 2024-01-30. global variance 3.9% vs billing (threshold 1%). mostly eu-west + dedicated tier. anyone else seeing this?

Grafana Bot: :rotating_light: Alert *unit_econ_reconciliation_variance* is firing
• window: 2024-01-30
• metric: (unit_econ_total_cost - billing_total_cost) / billing_total_cost
• value: 0.039
• top dims: region=eu-west tier=dedicated (0.061)
• dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/unit-econ-recon?from=1706582400000&to=1706668799000

Nadia Rahman: looking. first guess: late metering events or region mapping drift again. can someone paste the reconciliation job run id?

Cole Summers: run id `recon_job_2024-01-30T08:10Z` (airflow task `unit_econ_reconcile_daily`). logs here: https://console.redwood.ai/internal/airflow/log?dag=unit_econ_reconcile_daily&run=recon_job_2024-01-30T08:10Z

Logan Wright: i’m on it. checking raw partitions for `unit_econ_daily_v1` and `billing_metering_daily`.
quick query shows output_tokens look low on unit-econ side for eu-west/dedicated compared to metering, but *cost* is also off (unit-econ cost higher) which is weird.

Mei Lin: if unit-econ cost higher + tokens lower, could be missing late tokens but still allocating compute overhead? like allocation table joined but request events missing.

Thomas Baird: +1. the aggregation job allocates fleet cost by gpu_seconds / token counts at the same grain. if token side has holes, $/1M blows up + recon looks like “over-costed”.

Allison Grant: any indication ingestion lag is elevated? we had some kafka hiccups in eu-west yesterday.

Aisha Bello: checking freshness SLO dashboard. ingestion lag for `metering_events` peaked ~2h around 06:40Z eu-west. screenshot: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/telemetry-freshness/metering?var_region=eu-west

Nadia Rahman: ok that tracks. are the unit-econ rollups excluding late events or are we finalizing partitions too early?

Logan Wright: looks like we “finalize” the daily partition at 07:00Z, but eu-west metering lag means some events arrive after finalize and don’t get picked up unless backfill.
recon job is comparing finalized unit-econ partition vs billing totals that *do* include late events (billing pipeline holds window longer).

Cole Summers: so short-term: exclude last N hours / mark partition incomplete?

Thomas Baird: we can mitigate by changing recon comparator to skip partitions where `max(event_ingest_ts) - partition_end` > threshold, or just skip “today-1” until we’re past the late window.

Mei Lin: we already have late-event watermark in `telemetry_ingestion_watermarks` table. can the recon job gate on that?

Logan Wright: yup. there’s a field `is_complete` we can use but it’s not wired to recon.
for immediate mitigation today: in recon job config, exclude partitions with `partition_date >= current_date - 1` for eu-west OR exclude any partition where completeness < 99.5%.

Allison Grant: i’m ok with skipping last 24h in recon as a stopgap. better than paging everyone.

Aisha Bello: for alerts, we can also add a condition: only alert when completeness >= 99.5% AND variance > threshold. otherwise route to #data-quality as warning.

Cole Summers: :thumbsup: but we still need Finance to trust this. let’s confirm it’s *only* late events.
can someone validate by rerunning unit-econ aggregation for eu-west with extended lookback and see if variance drops?

Nadia Rahman: i can do a one-off backfill for `2024-01-30` eu-west partitions with late window = 6h.
command (dry-run first):
```
uecon backfill \
  --date 2024-01-30 \
  --region eu-west \
  --include-late-events \
  --late-window-hours 6 \
  --dry-run
```

Mei Lin: before backfill, check if any duplicate metering events got reprocessed. that can also cause billing higher. but Aisha’s lag graph suggests missing-in-uecon not extra-in-billing.

Logan Wright: i sampled request_ids present in billing metering but absent in uecon. many have ingest_ts ~07:35-08:20Z (post finalize). so it’s late arrivals.

Chloe Martin: does this affect dashboard users today? (Console internal unit-econ view)

Cole Summers: yes, if someone looks at “yesterday” eu-west/dedicated they’ll see elevated $/1M and lower tokens. need to note this in #announcements once mitigated.

Thomas Baird: for quick mitigation in semantic layer: we can filter out partitions where `is_complete=false` so UI doesn’t show incomplete day, or show banner “data still finalizing”.

Chloe Martin: please do. hiding partial day is preferable to showing wrong spikes.

Nadia Rahman: backfill dry-run says it will add ~18.7M output tokens and adjust allocated compute down per token. i’ll run real backfill now.

Nadia Rahman: ran it. partition reprocessed. next step: rerun recon job for that day.

Cole Summers: rerunning recon for 2024-01-30 only.

Cole Summers: update: variance now 0.6% global, eu-west/dedicated 0.9%. back within threshold. root cause = finalize cutoff too aggressive relative to eu-west lag.

Allison Grant: great. action items:
1) change recon alert gating on completeness
2) change unit-econ aggregation finalize window for eu-west (or globally) to +6h
3) UI/semantic layer exclude incomplete partitions / banner

Aisha Bello: i’ll open a ticket for (1) + update SLO doc to reflect “final” window. also add warning alert when completeness < 99.5% for yesterday.

Logan Wright: i’ll take (2) in pipeline. likely update scheduler so daily partitions finalize at 12:00Z, and keep incremental updates until then.

Thomas Baird: i’ll handle (3) guardrail in the query layer: default filter `is_complete=true` unless user explicitly toggles “include partial data”.

Cole Summers: i’ll post a short note to Finance channel + link the grafana recon view and say today’s spike was late partitions. thanks everyone.

Chloe Martin: +1. please also add to runbook: if recon spikes, first check ingestion lag + completeness before assuming cost allocation bug.

Nadia Rahman: i’ll update the backfill runbook with this exact scenario + commands. also: we should persist the late-window used per partition as metadata so it’s auditable.

Cole Summers: closing the loop here. :white_check_mark: mitigation in place: recon alert temporarily ignores partitions where completeness < 99.5% (Logan pushed config). we’ll follow up with proper finalize window change this week.
